Sofia — thanks for the clear ask. We're putting a short design note together and attaching a diagram (opsone-ephemeral-flow-v1.png) plus a draft runbook for forced rotation. High level answers first:

1) Tenant key material: never persisted in plaintext on the proxy. The proxy performs an in-memory wrapping operation using a short-lived session key (EPK) that is itself wrapped by the customer's HSM key (BYOK). The EPK lifecycle is ephemeral (TTL configurable, default 1 hour) and stored only in memory with strict OS-level mlock + process isolation.

2) Revocation path: operator credentials and ephemeral tokens are issued by our local control-plane auth broker (OIDC + mTLS). We support immediate revocation via: a) token blacklist push to the proxy control-plane, b) HSM key version disable (HSM side), and c) network-level egress block via your NAT gateway rules. The runbook includes the sequence for each path.

3) Egress policing: proxy binds to a single egress interface and validates destination by certificate + IP allowlist. We recommend a dedicated egress NAT gateway with static IPs and a strict ACL on your perimeter (we'll help generate the ACL CIDRs based on the attached spreadsheet).

I'll hand over to Logan for the sequence diagram and a suggested config snippet for the proxy and the HSM bridge. We'll also propose a rehearsal date for the forced rotation drill.

Best,

Subject: Re: BYO ephemeral token lifecycle & egress policing for private proxy — sequence & config

Folks — quick tech dive following Connor's note. Sequence (simple):

1) Tenant agent on-prem (client) asks Redwood control-plane for a short-lived wrap-token (signed JWT) bound to the client nonce and proxy instance id. Issued TTL = 15m by default.
2) Proxy receives the JWT, performs local attestation check (TPM quote or SGX attestation) and exchanges the JWT for an ephemeral EPK via an mTLS call to the control-plane auth-broker.
3) Proxy uses EPK to perform an in-memory AES-GCM wrap of tenant key material; then calls the HSM bridge to perform final wrap under the customer's BYOK KEK (HSM wrapping key). HSM returns wrapped blob and wrapping metadata (key_version, hw_nonce).
4) Wrapped blob is stored in the customer's sealed object store (encrypted-at-rest) or immediately transmitted to the destination HSM endpoint per customer preference. The unwrapped material never touches disk.

Revocation notes:
- Token revocation: the auth-broker maintains a revoke-list; proxies poll every 30s (or subscribe via push) and invalidate any active EPKs matching revoked tokens.
- HSM key disable: we provide an API shim to request immediate HSM KEK disable; this is a hard-fail for any new unwrap operations and is recorded in the audit log.
- Network fail-safe: if egress ACLs are updated to block our egress IPs, any outbound wrap/transfer calls fail fast and the proxy drops the EPK from memory.

Config snippet (example proxy YAML):
proxy:
  egress_interface: eth1
  egress_allowlist: ["198.51.100.23/32"]
  attest_method: tpm_v2
  epk_ttl_seconds: 3600
  token_poll_interval_seconds: 30
  control_plane_endpoint: https://auth-broker.redwood.internal
  hsm_bridge_endpoint: https://hsm-bridge.local:8443

Operational rehearsal (proposal): 2026-11-18 09:00-10:30 PST — forced token revoke + HSM key disable + network egress block. We will run in the EdgeBank staging VPC.

Logan Wright

Sofia / team — answers inline and next steps: 

- Attestation CA: yes — on install we can provision your attestation root and the proxy will validate and present TPM quotes signed by your CA. We'll document the bootstrapping steps in the runbook.

- SIEM push SLA: we provide a push endpoint that supports batched JSON events over HTTPS. In our staging tests we've achieved sub-2-minute delivery for individual wrap events; 5 minutes for ingestion is well within capability. We'll include a sample webhook consumer and schema in the runbook.

- Breakglass flow (summary):
  1) Create emergency request via the control-plane UI (requires two named approvers).
  2) Auth-broker issues a short-lived emergency unwrap token (valid 10 minutes) with the request id embedded.
  3) Emergency unwrap calls are logged to immutable audit storage and a signed certificate of the operation is emitted.
  4) Post-event: automated report generated and pushed to your Jira project.
